title: Jurassic Park
facts: Steven Spielberg directed the film, from Michael Crichton's 1990 novel.
Michael Crichton and David Koepp wrote the screenplay.
Jurassic Park won three Academy Awards: Sound, Sound Effects Editing, and Visual Effects.
Stan Winston's studio built the full-size animatronic dinosaurs. Industrial Light & Magic made the digital ones.
Location filming took place on the Hawaiian island of Kauai. Hurricane Iniki struck during the shoot in September 1992.
The T. rex roar blends several animal sounds, including a baby elephant.
Jurassic Park became the highest-grossing film of its time. Titanic passed it a few years later.
John Hammond was Richard Attenborough's first acting role in more than a decade.
Phil Tippett is credited as "Dinosaur Supervisor".
Jurassic Park opened in the United States on June 11, 1993.
Spielberg oversaw post-production while he filmed Schindler's List in Poland.
In 2018 the Library of Congress selected Jurassic Park for the National Film Registry.
The park is on Isla Nublar, a fictional island off the coast of Costa Rica.
Samuel L. Jackson plays the park's chief engineer, Ray Arnold.
The film's Velociraptors are much larger than the real animal, and closer in size to Deinonychus.
